audits.mathematicalReason: The regular hexagon has interior angles of 120°. In the displayed configuration, each inward indentation is a 120° arc, while each outward lobe consists of two such arcs and spans 240°. Thus each of the nine congruent arcs has angle 120°, and its length 2π/3 gives radius r = 1. The side-2 hexagon consists of six equilateral triangles and has area 6√3. Relative to this hexagon, add three outward 240° sectors and subtract three inward 120° sectors: area = 6√3 + 3(2π/3) − 3(π/3) = 6√3 + π. Sector-area addition and subtraction is the assessed procedure; all listed supporting scopes have valid roles in this method.

figureEvidence.fact: The six marked centers alternate between three centers inside outward lobes and three centers outside the shaded region beside inward indentations.

Neighboring circular portions meet smoothly between adjacent marked centers. The resulting joins are side midpoints of the center hexagon, giving the 120° inward sectors and 240° outward lobes used in the decomposition.

audits.mathematicalReason: Cities C and E have degree two and are not endpoints, so their roads must be traversed as the passages B–C–D and A–E–D. Suppressing these cities leaves two distinguishable A–D connections, two distinguishable D–B connections, and one A–B connection. The exhaustive reduced vertex patterns are A–B–D–A–D–B, A–D–A–B–D–B, A–D–B–A–D–B, and A–D–B–D–A–B. Each pattern permits 2! assignments of the A–D connections and 2! assignments of the D–B connections. Hence there are 4 × 2 × 2 = 16 routes. Degree-based graph reasoning and combined addition/multiplication counting directly fit the two assessed scopes.

figureEvidence.fact: The figure has exactly the seven stated roads: AB, AD, AE, BC, BD, CD, and DE. In particular, C is incident only to BC and CD, and E only to AE and DE.

audits.mathematicalReason: Each original arc is a radius-2 quarter-circle. Complete the displayed star to a square whose sides pass through its four tips; this square has side length 4. Its complement outside the star consists of four radius-2 quarter-circle sectors, one at each corner. Therefore the star has area 16 − 4π, while the original circle has area 4π. The ratio is (16 − 4π)/(4π) = (4 − π)/π. The square-minus-sectors construction is a valid composite-area method, with sector area substantive and square and circle areas supporting.

figureEvidence.fact: The original circle is divided at four equally spaced points, producing quarter-circle arcs.

The reassembled star has four axial tips and four inward-bending quarter-circle sides. Completing it to the surrounding square places the tips at side midpoints and the sector centers at square corners.

audits.mathematicalReason: The Pythagorean theorem gives AC = √(1² + 2²) = √5. Since AD is the internal angle bisector, BD/DC = AB/AC = 1/√5. Writing BD = x and DC = 2 − x gives x/(2 − x) = 1/√5, so x = 2/(1 + √5) = (√5 − 1)/2. This value is positive and less than BC = 2. The side-ratio theorem is the assessed step, with the Pythagorean theorem and denominator rationalization supporting it.

figureEvidence.fact: The right-angle marker is at B, and D lies strictly between B and C on segment BC. Segment AD is drawn inside triangle ABC.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the common small-square side length be s. The two upper corner squares leave a horizontal gap of length 1 − 2s between their inward-facing vertices. Those vertices are midpoints of adjacent sides of the central square. Their distance, by the Pythagorean theorem applied to two perpendicular half-sides, is √((s/2)² + (s/2)²) = s/√2. Hence 1 − 2s = s/√2, giving s = 1/(2 + 1/√2) = (4 − √2)/7. Thus a = 4, b = 7, and a + b = 11. Square properties and the Pythagorean theorem are substantive steps, with rationalization supporting the requested answer form.

figureEvidence.fact: Four small squares occupy the four corners of the unit square, with their sides aligned with its boundary.
The inward-facing vertices of the two upper corner squares are horizontally aligned and coincide with midpoints of adjacent sides of the tilted central square.

audits.mathematicalReason: External tangency makes every center-to-center distance 2 + 2 = 4, so the centers form an equilateral triangle of area 4√3. Inside that triangle, the three circles occupy three 60° sectors whose total area is 3 × (60/360) × π × 2² = 2π. The central gap therefore has area 4√3 − 2π. Adding it to the three full circle areas gives 12π + 4√3 − 2π = 10π + 4√3. Sector subtraction is the central assessed procedure, and the listed circle-position, equilateral-triangle, Pythagorean, triangle-area, and circle-area scopes all support this method.

figureEvidence.fact: The three equal circles are pairwise externally tangent, with disjoint interiors.
The shading includes all three disks and the small curvilinear triangular gap between them.

routes.label: Split into an equilateral triangle and parallelogram

audits.mathematicalReason: Let each leg have length l and the shorter base AD have length x. Dropping altitudes shows that each leg contributes a horizontal projection l/2, so BC = x + l. The perimeter condition is therefore 2x + 3l = 30. Positivity gives 1 ≤ l ≤ 9, and integrality of x forces l to be even. Thus l = 2, 4, 6, or 8, yielding (AD, BC) = (12,14), (9,13), (6,12), or (3,11). Each produces a positive-height trapezoid uniquely determined up to congruence, and the four are distinct. The alternative equilateral-triangle/parallelogram cut also proves BC − AD = l. Both optional geometric routes are defensible alternatives; their union is not required. Bounded integer enumeration and parity fit the assessed and supporting scopes.

figureEvidence.fact: AD and BC are the parallel bases, with AD the shorter upper base. The equal-leg marks are on AB and DC, and the two lower interior angles are marked 60°.

audits.mathematicalReason: Place the rectangle at 0 ≤ x ≤ 8 and 0 ≤ y ≤ 5. The crossing segments join (1,5) to (7,0), and (0,4) to (8,1). Each endpoint pair is centrally symmetric about O = (4,5/2), so both segments pass through O. Split the upper-left shaded quadrilateral along the segment from its rectangle corner to O. Its two triangles have areas (1 × 5/2)/2 = 5/4 and (1 × 4)/2 = 2, totaling 13/4. The lower-right shaded quadrilateral is its half-turn image, so the total shaded area is 2 × 13/4 = 13/2. Composite triangulation is the assessed procedure; central symmetry and triangle area provide the stated support.

figureEvidence.fact: The top edge is divided into lengths 1 and 7, while the bottom edge is divided into 7 and 1. The left edge is divided into 1 above and 4 below, while the right edge is divided into 4 above and 1 below.

The crossing segments connect the top division point to the bottom division point and the left division point to the right division point. The shaded regions are the upper-left and lower-right corner quadrilaterals.
